name: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner
bio: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner was a German expressionist painter and printmaker. He was one of the founders of the artists group Die Brücke or "The Bridge", a key group leading to the foundation of Expressionism in 20th-century art. Kirchner volunteered for army service in the First World War, but soon suffered a breakdown and was discharged. His work was branded as "degenerate" by the Nazis in 1937 and more than 600 of his works were sold or destroyed.

paintings.title: Berlin Street Scene
paintings.story: Berlin Street Scene is a 1913 painting from the cycle Street scenes, by the German expressionist artist Ernst Ludwig Kirchner. The cycle, created by Kirchner between 1913 and 1915, often depicts "Kokotten" (prostitutes) with their clients, and is regarded as one of the most important works of German Expressionism.
facts: After that the painting was sold by the auction house Christie's for 30 million Euros (approximately USD$38 million) to the art collectors Ronald Lauder and Serge Sabarsky.
The restitution was based on the Washington Declaration from 1998 in which Germany said it would return the paintings that were confiscated during the Nazi era to the heirs of the victims.

paintings.title: Female Half-Length Nude with Hat
paintings.story: Female Half-Length Nude with Hat is an 1911 oil on canvas painting by the German Expressionist painter Ernst Ludwig Kirchner. It is currently held at the Museum Ludwig in Cologne.
facts: The painting was originally part of the Adolphe Basler collection in Paris and was later acquired by the American art dealer Sam Salz who was living in Paris at the time.
It survived the Nazi era there and was donated to the Wallraf-Richartz Museum in Cologne in 1946, along with the entire Haubrich collection.

paintings.title: Self-Portrait as a Soldier
paintings.story: Self-Portrait as a Soldier, or Selbstbildnis als Soldat, is an Expressionist oil-on-canvas painting by the German artist Ernst Ludwig Kirchner. Kirchner created this self-depiction in 1915, following his medical discharge from military service during the First World War. The artwork measures 69 centimetres in height by 61 centimetres in width. The painting was first exhibited in the 'Städtische Galerie' in Germany between 1916 and 1919 and currently resides at the Allen Memorial Art Museum in Ohio USA. Critical interpretations of the painting attribute its stark Expressionist style and myriad of symbolic elements to the socio-political turbulence of Germany during the First World War. Self Portrait as a Soldier may be viewed as testimony to Kirchner's volatile mental and physical health and as a critique of the chaotic instability of Germany during the early 20th century.
facts: "Primitive Art", pertaining to the art and ritual objects of ancient cultures, notably from African or Central Asian regions, was as great passion of Kirchner's and a further reason for the denunciation of his art as 'degenerate' during the Nazi regime.
The Nazi regime, active in Germany from 1933 to 1945, upheld a strong anti-Bolshevik agenda which amounted to vehement rejection of modern art.

paintings.title: Portrait of Erna Schilling
paintings.story: Portrait of Erna Schilling, also known as Sick Woman or Woman with an Hat, is an oil-on-canvas painting executed in 1913 by the German Expressionist artist Ernst Ludwig Kirchner. It depicts the nightclub dancer Erna Schilling, from Berlin, who after Kirchner's move from Dresden to Berlin in 1911, became his friend and model, and later, common-law wife. The portrait shows Kirchner's signature on the top left: EL Kirchner. It has been in the collection of the National Gallery, in Berlin, since 1989.
facts: Hidden in the Frankfurt Städel with the entire Hagemann collection, the work survived the Nazi era.
After moving from Dresden to Berlin in October 1911, Kirchner met the dancer Erna Schilling and her sister Gerda in a Berlin nightclub.

paintings.title: Street, Berlin (Kirchner)
paintings.story: Street, Berlin is an oil painting by Ernst Ludwig Kirchner painted in 1913 before the outbreak of World War I. At this time, Kirchner painted several different street scenes that illustrated the chaos of city life and the relationship between men and women.
facts: Street, Berlin depicts a busy street scene as men and women walk down the sidewalk.
Two women in the central foreground are the focal point of the piece.

paintings.title: Alpine Kitchen
paintings.story: Alpine Kitchen is an oil painting on canvas by German artist Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, executed in 1918. It was made when the painter was temporarily living in a mountain hut in the Alps, at 1900 meters of height, above Davos. The house still exists almost in his original form. The painting came from Kirchner's estate and today belongs to the collection of the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum in Madrid.
facts: It is signed, with a small signature at the bottom right that reads EL Kirchner and on the back is the name KN-Da/Ad2.
It was exhibited in Frankfurt/Main in 1922 and in Berlin in 1926.

paintings.title: Archers (Kirchner)
paintings.story: Archers is an oil-on-canvas painting by German painter Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, created in 1935–1937, at his Swiss home town of Davos. It belongs to his last phase, in which he abandoned the Expressionism of his earlier work. The painting depicts three people engaged in the sport of archery. On the back it bears the signature EL Kirchner. The painting is part of the collection of the Kirchner Museum Davos.
facts: A female figure in the foreground holds arrows in her hands, while the male figure on the left drawns the bow.
What they all have in common is their concentrated gaze directed at the target.

paintings.title: The Red Tower in Halle
paintings.story: The Red Tower in Halle is an oil-on-canvas painting by the German expressionist painter Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, executed in 1915. It is now housed at Museum Folkwang, Essen.
facts: The painting shows the market square in the town of Halle with the Red Tower.
The 15th-century neo-Gothic bell tower surmounts a red brick building.

paintings.title: The Bridge near Wiesen
paintings.story: The Bridge near Wiesen, also known as The Bridge at Wiesen, is an oil-on-canvas painting by the German painter Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, from 1926. It depicts the Wiesen Viaduct, south of Davos, in Switzerland. It is signed on the bottom right of the center and is dated '26' on the back. The painting is held at the Kirchner Museum Davos.
facts: In 1933, at the instigation of the art-loving Landammann Erhard Branger, the municipality of Davos acquired the painting Rathaus Davos Platz, directly from Kirchner, after lengthy purchase negotiations, and despite some resistance from the population.
In the years 1925/1926, a stylistic change started to appear in Kirchner's work.

paintings.title: Five Bathing Women at a Lake
paintings.story: Five Bathing at a Lake is an oil-on-canvas painting by the Expressionist German painter Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, from 1911. It depicts five nude women, in different poses, near a lake, four of them with their feet already in the water. The painting is in the Brücke Museum, in Berlin.
